messages:
Nina: opening a small PR to slim down the Quickstart hello-world (JS + Python). goal: remove deprecated flags, unify auth var, and collapse the multi-stage Dockerfile into a single easy-to-follow example. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2401. can @Raj or @Theo eyeball?
Raj: Thanks. Quick skim: we should keep a one-line curl for power users but lead with SDK examples. Also, the current py snippet uses `from redwood import Client` which is old api. new SDK exposes `RedwoodClient`.
Theo: yup, switch to RedwoodClient. Also please add a tiny migration note: "If you were using redwood==0.x, update imports and init call." People will hit import errors during onboarding.
Nina: good catch. i will update the py snippet to: `from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))` and add a 1-line migration blurb.
doc-bot: /docs/lint report: PR 2401 - code fence language missing on one snippet, broken link to /v1beta/old-auth in one place.
Nina: fixing both. i'll add language tags and point link to /guides/auth (per redirect).
Raj: on Docker: the current multi-stage used `--platform=linux/amd64` which is unnecessary and confuses arm users. remove platform flag and add a note: "If you need a specific architecture, see advanced builds." Keep the Dockerfile tiny: FROM node:18-alpine, copy package.json, install, add the single start command.
Theo: small stylistic suggestion: avoid claiming exact minutes ("5-minute setup"); use "Quickstart: get a local run in minutes". also add a short troubleshooting bullet: "If you get ENOENT when running `npm start`, check that you copied the example env file and set REDWOOD_API_KEY."
Nina: will do. adding troubleshooting, replacing the time claim, and simplifying Dockerfile. also keeping a single curl example and marking it as "advanced / quick-check" so it's not the recommended path.
QA: small test note: can we include a quick smoke test command that CI can use? e.g. `npm run smoke` that hits `/health` or makes a one-off generate call. saves time when validating docs changes.
Raj: good idea. add a tiny script in package.json named "smoke" that runs `node smoke.js` which does a quick generate. we can link to how to set env vars for CI.
Nina: added smoke command and a one-line smoke.js snippet. also updated the examples to use `REDWOOD_API_KEY` consistently and added a table mapping legacy env var `REDWOOD_KEY` -> `REDWOOD_API_KEY` for users on older versions.
doc-bot: /docs/lint re-run: now only warns about line length in the example long prompt; consider truncating the sample prompt to one sentence.
Theo: replace long prompt with "Write a friendly greeting". keeps output predictable.
Nina: done. updated prompt and pushed commit (https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/commit/5b2c8ef).
QA: ran the smoke script locally with a dev key, worked. just one nit: the py example prints `response.text` but the new client returns `response.output[0].text` in newest SDK. we should show a safe access pattern to avoid index errors.
Nina: adjusted py and js to use a safe accessor: `const out = res.output?.[0]?.text ?? res.text` and similar in py.
Raj: approving from docs side. small wording nit: change "legacy users" to "older SDKs" in the table header.
Nina: changed that phrase.
doc-bot: /docs/lint 10/10 checks passed. PR auto-merge scheduled after CI.
Theo: thanks all. once merged can we backport the migration blurb to the migration guide? i'll open a follow-up to copy the blurb into /guides/migration.
Nina: yep i'll cherry-pick the blurb into that guide and ping you. thanks team. :sparkles:
